coasterslaunchsystems.ponder.controller_: Mount both anchors on floor supports so they face up, then place modules beside the level rail.
Use the Span Tool on two coaster anchors in travel order, then use it on the controller.
Shift-use the controller with the tool selected, then use the tool on each bound module to link it.
Inspect bindings and safety hardware before arming. A loaded controller or cabinet always comes back disarmed.
coasterslaunchsystems.ponder.linear_moto: LSM and LIM use separate cabinets and matching reaction plates. Do not mix their plates.
Install the matching plate on the certified chassis interface, then bind the cabinet over level fixed rail.
Charge with a real Create shaft and tune while empty and disarmed. Linear braking cannot provide a static hold.
coasterslaunchsystems.ponder.brake_hardw: A spring fin clamp uses the chassis brake fin for final stop and hold.
The magnetic brake uses the conductive fin and dissipates motion; it does not hold a stopped train.
Skid hardware needs its matching shoe. Bind every cabinet to its local span and leave a friction hold downstream.
coasterslaunchsystems.ponder.cable_launc: Install a chassis socket and a continuous guide five blocks below straight, level rail. The bound controller installs the physical carriage.
Bind one finite-energy cable cabinet, a powered home fin, and a downstream fin stop. The 12-block pull needs a 20-block guide.
The flywheel spends stored rotation during the pull. The catch releases before its end stop; shaft power returns the carriage before reset.
Shaft power charges the pump or compressor. Hydraulic oil returns to its reservoir; pneumatic force falls as the receiver expands. Stored pressure can finish a pull with the shaft stopped.
After a restart, inspect the retained catch and guide. At home, use the Span Tool with an offhand redstone torch to release onto linked fin clamps; an offhand compass retires the idle carriage.
